summary: Peered VPC route-table propagation mismatch causes control-plane auth loop via corporate proxy 407 responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that their Private deployment control plane entered a sustained authentication retry loop after a scheduled peering change between two AWS accounts. The control-plane agents show repeated 407 Proxy Authentication Required responses when attempting token refresh and artifact fetches, which triggers accelerated retry backoff and a surge of outbound attempts.

Impact:
- Agent heartbeats from ~40 serving nodes in customer us-east private deployment were intermittently marked unhealthy and cycled (30-60s).
- Model pulls timed out intermittently causing request errors (429/502 depending on path).
- Customer reports production traffic >5% error rate for 45 minutes during peak hours.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbus Retail Inc. (private deployment, VPC peering between account A and B)
- Redwood Private control plane (managed) in us-east-1
- Agents running on customer-managed serving nodes in peered VPC (account B)
- Corporate egress proxy sits in account A and is expected to handle outbound web auth for peered subnets

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Customer applied new route table to peered VPC (account B) that removed explicit propagation for the control-plane CIDR and replaced with a 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop to a customer appliance.
2) Agents attempted token refresh to control-plane endpoint (controlplane.redwood.internal -> resolved to IP in account A).
3) Packets from serving hosts in account B were routed to the appliance in account B (0.0.0.0/0) instead of traversing the peering path to account A, creating asymmetric path and hitting the corporate web-proxy cluster that expects requests to be authenticated via a different header exchange.
4) Proxy returned 407 responses; agents retried rapidly due to our token-refresh backoff being reset by the intermittent 407s, leading to a storm of auth attempts and control-plane retries.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Agent logs (serving-node-12): "token_refresh: received 407 Proxy Authentication Required; proxy-id=corp-proxy-7; content='Proxy-Authenticate: Negotiate'"
- Control plane logs: "auth: token invalidation from 10.12.5.20: excessive retries -> escalate"
- VPC flow logs: show SYN->RST from appliance IP for control-plane target IP; no direct peering path entries for account B->account A after route change.

Hypothesis:
Route table update in customer account B created a default route that diverted traffic destined for the control plane through a local appliance/proxy rather than the VPC peering path. The corporate proxy inserts/mandates an authentication handshake (407) that our agents don't perform, resulting in failed token refreshes and retry storms. Asymmetric routing also caused some TCP session resets for artifact downloads.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed route table in account B now has 0.0.0.0/0 -> appliance ENI and no explicit routes for control-plane CIDR; peering connection still exists and routes were previously propagated.
- Customer's network team admits they toggled route propagation as part of a security baseline change; they believed traffic to account A would still prefer peering due to local route priority but omitted the explicit CIDR entry.
- Turned on DEBUG on agent token refresh path; agents do not attempt Proxy-Authenticate flows and treat 407 as a failure class similar to 4xx.
- Verified that when we manually injected a host route (control-plane CIDR -> peering ENI) from customer side, agent heartbeats returned to normal and token refresh succeeded.

Customer communications:
- 2026-03-10 10:22 UTC: Notified customer we are investigating; requested recent route table and peering acceptance logs.
- 2026-03-10 10:45 UTC: Customer confirmed they applied a baseline route policy 10:30 UTC.
- 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC: Provided mitigation steps to add explicit host route for control-plane CIDR; customer applied host route at 11:12 UTC.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Customer added explicit route for control-plane CIDR (172.20.64.0/21) -> peering connection.
- We issued a soft-throttle on agent token refresh backoff logic for customer cluster to avoid token-storm (configuration change on control plane to raise retry jitter for 20 minutes).

Root cause:
- Route-propagation change on customer's side removed explicit control-plane prefix route, causing asymmetric egress through corporate appliance that enforces proxy auth. Agents do not perform proxy authentication, so token refreshes fail with 407 and trigger retry storms.

Resolution / next steps:
1) Customer restored explicit route to peering for control-plane CIDR (immediate resolution).
2) Networking runbook updated (confluence) to require explicit CIDR route for Redwood control-plane prefixes when applying route propagation changes. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/5021/Peering+Runbook
3) Follow-up: engineering to add a defensive check in agent startup that validates direct reachability to control-plane IPs and warns if a proxy is in-path. Tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1482 (owner: @liamoc).
4) Recommend customer add an egress-scope ACL that allows peering CIDR -> control-plane CIDR priority above default appliance route.

Impact window and timeline:
- 2026-03-10 10:30-11:15 UTC: peak errors; mitigation applied 11:12 UTC, full healthy state by 11:25 UTC.

Notes for postmortem: include suggestion to extend agent telemetry to detect 407/407-like proxy signs sooner and surface a clear "proxy-in-path" alert in Console.
